paper_title: Simple Constructions of Linear-Depth t-Designs and Pseudorandom Unitaries
authors: Tony Metger (ETH Zurich, Switzerland), Alexander Poremba (MIT, USA), Makrand Sinha (University of Illinois, USA), Henry Yuen (Columbia University, USA)
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 4
statement: c) Pseudorandom isometries with adaptive security: We conjecture that our PRU construction is also adaptively secure, but so far we are not able to prove adaptive security for the case of unitaries. However, we can show adaptive security under a small relaxation: if instead of PRUs, we consider PRIs that map n qubits to n + ω(log n) qubits, then we can show adaptive security. Our PRI construction is the same as our PRU construction, with two minor differences: we fix part of the input state to the |+⟩-state (which is what makes this an isometry) and we do not require the random Clifford.
context: Corollary (informal). For any number of qubits n, tolerated error ϵ > 0, and t ≤ 2n/4 , there exists a diamond ϵ-approximate t-design with circuit size and depth O(t · poly(n) + t log 1/ϵ) and a relative-error ϵ-approximate tdesign with circuit size and depth O(t2 · poly(n) + t2 log 1/ϵ). c) Pseudorandom isometries with adaptive security: We conjecture that our PRU construction is also adaptively secure, but so far we are not able to prove adaptive security for the case of unitaries. However, we can show adaptive security under a small relaxation: if instead of PRUs, we consider PRIs that map n qubits to n + ω(log n) qubits, then we can show adaptive security. Our PRI construction is the same as our PRU construction, with two minor differences: we fix part of the input state to the |+⟩-state (which is what makes this an isometry) and we do not require the random Clifford. In fact, as mentioned before, the upcoming work [6] gives explicit circuits for the O(t)-wise independent permutations from [19] that also achieve quasilinear depth in n, which implies t-designs in depth Õ(tn) (for diamond distance error ϵ = e−Ω(n) ). b) Computational derandomisation: non-adaptive pseudorandom unitaries: Replacing the uniformly random function and permutation in the P F C ensemble with their pseudorandom counterparts, we immediately get a PRU ensemble with non-adaptive security.
